bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Device, InputSet, Decoder), springboard/src/bare/pointer_finger.rs, springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs (Input enum)
summary: BifrOSt reads human interface devices (keyboards, touch, pointers, lid and jack switches) through Linux evdev in the system layer, and writes synthetic evdev events. Apps get decoded key and touch events but no HID report, element or stylus API, and there is no SDK for authoring a device driver; DriverKit driver authoring is treated as n/a for a desktop SDK because the Linux kernel owns drivers.

features.feature: Driver authoring (HIDDriverKit C++ driver classes, system extension packaging)
features.bifrost: none; drivers are Linux kernel drivers
features.note: A user-space driver model for a desktop SDK is not planned; the Linux kernel owns HID drivers

Runs in the shell; apps never open devices. Blocker: Device::open takes an exclusive grab, so an app reader would receive no events, and the shell's decoded keys and touches reach apps through the runtime input enum instead.

features.feature: Device discovery and matching by capability
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 5 (w5-hiddriverkit, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Matching is by evdev capability, not by HID usage pairs; no app-facing matching API

features.apple: Handling Keyboard Events from a Human Interface Device, kIOHIDSupportedKeyboardUsagePairsKey
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:16-18 (Key, Switch events), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:20-28 (Input::Key), springboard/src/bare/key_usage.rs (usage_of, code_of, boot_modifier_bit, boot_report)
features.note: Key events stay evdev codes, and key_usage maps them to HID keyboard usages (page 0x07) with a boot keyboard report and roll-over, tested in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-complete-46.rs. Gap: no keyboard usage-pair declaration is published to the system, and keys outside the boot set (keypad, media, vendor keys) have no usage.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:63-65 (protocol B decoder, first contact only), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:21 (Input::Touch)
features.note: Only slot 0 is tracked; no digitizer collection or per-contact data for apps

features.apple: IOHIDDigitizerStylusData, Handling Stylus Input from a Human Interface Device
features.note: Pure model in bifrost_ui::stylus: pressure maps to force, tilt maps to altitude and azimuth, and hover reports are skipped. These mappings are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-07-w7.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell and not tested on the VM or Midget. No device decoding; the eraser flag is carried on the report but to_point does not act on it.

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/device_match.rs (Criteria::pointer, Capabilities); springboard/src/bare/pointer_finger.rs (Mouse, PointerFinger), springboard/src/bare/input.rs:382 (PointerDecoder), :656 (pointer source selection)
features.note: A pointer device is matched by capability (relative motion and a left button), tested headless in parity_sdk-os-01. Gap: scroll wheel axes are not a matching criterion, and no app reads pointer events.

Lid, tablet mode and headset states, their edges, and per-observer SwitchWatch selection are tested headless in ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-37.rs. Gap: the shell does not yet publish switch edges to apps, and the feed needs the tablet or Midget hardware.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/input.rs:205-207 (writes a one-finger swipe or tap into an evdev node)
features.note: Only touch gestures are synthesised, for test and automation; no app-facing virtual device API

features.feature: Raw HID report and element access for apps
features.apple: IOHIDElement, HID Usage Tables, Low-Level Information
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API exposes HID report elements or usage tables to apps

gaps: No app-facing API for raw HID reports, elements or usage tables
Stylus and pen data (pressure, tilt, eraser) is not decoded
Touch decoding tracks only the first contact (slot 0)
No app-facing device matching or hotplug notification by HID usage
Synthetic input exists only for touch gestures, with no general virtual HID device API
